newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 12.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- A man with a 20-year grudge was being hunted by the RUC and paramilitaries after he shot dead a former 'Shankill Butcher' in Belfast.
- The number of people seeking asylum in Ireland is expected to double this year to 5,000, putting enormous strain on services for the homeless.
- Twelve people were arrested yesterday as police and customs officers smashed a multi-million pound drug trafficking and money-laundering operation.
- Seagate, the giant U.S. electronics firm, is to provide 1,000 new jobs in Ringaskiddy in Cork over the next three years.
- The murder of the 'Shankill Butcher' Robert Bates is believed to have been a revenge killing carried out by a loyalist.
- The Northern Secretary Mo Mowlam has warned Sinn Fein that it can have one more meeting with British officials after which the so-called "settlement train" appears set to leave without it.
- A murder investigation has begun following the discovery of the body of a Malaysian woman in a house in Dublin.
- The Progressive Democrats are expected to get one senior cabinet position and two junior ministries from negotiations with Fianna Fail on the formation of a new coalition government.
- Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern will be faced with a hefty list of demands when he seeks the support of Independents in his attempt to be elected prime minister.

- A leading multinational electronics firm, Seagate Technology Inc, is to create more than 1,000 jobs in Cork after Ireland beat stiff international competition to bring the 150 million punt project to the region.
- Major changes are called for in a new report on pensions including a big increase in state pensions.
